LanguageData.CC_Hamlet_Ask_Holding: {LEADER} came up from {HOLDING} today with a question that had clearly been talked over for a while. A year on the colony's land has done them good, and they would like a place of their own now: {WORD} of {PEOPLE}, {WHERE}, at the place marked on the map.

LanguageData.CC_Hamlet_Ask_Refugees: {LEADER}'s family has gone back up the road to tell the others from {FROM}. If the colony takes them under its protection, they will make {WORD} {WHERE}, at the place marked on the map, instead of going on to strangers.
LanguageData.CC_Hamlet_Ask_How: Under {PROTECTION}, they would camp at the colony's gate with their carts until a caravan of the colony's sets out for the place, travel beside it, and light their first fires after a night there with it. They can wait at the gate only a few days. Alone, the road may turn them back. Once it stands, the hamlet would bring the colony some of its harvest, and would turn to it in hard times.

LanguageData.CC_SetNote_Hamlets: Settlers may ask to found a hamlet a few days off under the colony's protection, and in time swear fealty.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Hamlets_Tip: From the colony's 90th day, with five grown colonists or more at a home, settlers of a people at peace may ask to found a hamlet near it, at most once a year and one hamlet a home: a holding that has lived a year on the colony's land with little unease, the families of a town given up (offered at the gate), or settlers from a poor or struggling town in reach. The place is 6 to 10 tiles off, on land that holds a town, by a river or a road where it can; the colony may choose another. Taken under protection, they camp at the gate with their carts for a few days, and a caravan of two grown colonists or more sent to the place takes them along; after a night there the hamlet stands, a town of their own people. At the founding the road may bring the game's own caravan demand or ambush (15 in 100, 35 near a raiders' camp or a hostile town), with the settlers among the defenders. Let go alone, a third are turned back. The hamlet brings produce at harvest and asks for food, a doctor or tools in hard seasons; refused twice in one season, it stops counting on the colony. After 60 days at a fortune of 40 or more it asks to swear fealty (Faction Territories' vassal when its vassalage is on). Off: no settlers ask, and a hamlet standing goes on as a town of its people.
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_SmallTownMaps: A hamlet, a trading post or a town in its first year has a smaller base with fewer defenders on its own map.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_SmallTownMaps_Tip: When the map of a hamlet, a trading post or a town in its first year is made (attacked or entered), its base stands on smaller ground (a hamlet 0.6 of a town's on each side, a post 0.75, a new town 0.8) with fewer defenders (0.35, 0.5 and 0.65 of a town's) and less in its stores; a hamlet has no walls round its edge. With Vanilla Base Generation Expanded each people's own layouts are built on the smaller ground. An Empire town keeps its ground, with fewer defenders. Sites, ruins and other mods' world objects are never touched. Needs the deeper game hooks.
